note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  
  - Acute chest tightness for 3 hours  
  - Mild shortness of breath, worse on exertion (stairs), no shortness of breath at rest  
  - Wheezing and non-productive cough persisting after a recent viral upper respiratory infection (cold with sore throat, runny nose improving)  
  - Known asthma since childhood, not using inhalers for about 1 week due to running out  
  - History of severe asthma exacerbation at age 16–17 requiring intubation and hospital admission  
  - Allergies: dust allergy, hay fever  
  - Childhood eczema and milk protein allergy (resolved)  

- Relevant family medical history:  
  - Mother with eczema  
  - Father with asthma  

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  - Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – currently out of stock for ~1 week; dose/route/frequency not documented  
  - Clenil Modulite (inhaled corticosteroid) inhaler – currently out of stock for ~1 week; dose/route/frequency not documented  
  - Short course oral steroids prescribed (dose: two tablets in the morning for 5 days) during this consultation  

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded  

- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded  

- Physical activity and nutrition:  
  - Able to walk on flat surfaces without shortness of breath, mildly more breathless on stairs  

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded  

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded  

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  
  - Patient reports feeling scared of current symptoms but no formal mental health concerns documented  

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded  

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  
  - University student, recently away from home  
  - No mention of smoking or occupational exposures  

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded  
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Clinical impression strongly suggests asthma exacerbation triggered by recent viral illness and medication omission (no inhalers for ~1 week).  
- Symptoms consistent with asthma exacerbation: chest tightness, wheezing, shortness of breath on exertion, non-productive persistent cough.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript and supported by DDx:  
  1. Asthma exacerbation (High likelihood) – supported by history, known asthma, recent cessation of inhalers, and viral trigger.  
  2. Acute bronchitis (Moderate likelihood) – recent cold with residual cough and wheeze, but asthma history and medication noncompliance strongly favor asthma exacerbation.  
  3. Pulmonary embolism (Low likelihood) – symptoms overlap but no risk factors or clinical features to support this.  
- Anxiety/panic attack considered less likely due to objective wheezing and known asthma history but patient reports mild anxiety.  
- No conflict noted between transcript and DDx.  

Management Plan

- Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler and Clenil Modulite inhaler with instruction to resume regular Clenil Modulite in the morning and Ventolin PRN for wheezing.  
- Prescribed oral corticosteroids: two tablets each morning for five days to reduce airway inflammation.  
- Provided spacer device with instructions to optimize inhaler delivery; patient has used spacer but rarely. New spacer to be sent.  
- Advised to seek urgent medical attention if Ventolin use required more frequently than every 3 hours or if symptoms worsen, including chest pain, increased shortness of breath, or light-headedness.  
- Recommended rest and time off work; patient can self-certify first 7 days.  
- Patient education provided on steroid side effects and asthma management.  

Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded  
Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded  
Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded  
CTG registration: Not recorded  
Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Asthma exacerbation – High likelihood  
  Justification: Known asthma with recent medication omission, viral respiratory infection trigger, wheezing, chest tightness, mild exertional dyspnea, no severe rest symptoms.  
- Acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood  
  Justification: Recent respiratory infection with persistent cough and wheeze; less favored due to asthma history and medication nonadherence implicated.  
- Pulmonary embolism – Low likelihood  
  Justification: Acute chest tightness and dyspnea overlap, but no risk factors, pleuritic pain, or hemoptysis; young age and asthma history reduce likelihood.  

Quality checks:  
- Missing clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), anthropometric data (height, weight, BMI), immunization status review, alcohol/tobacco/substance use history, mental health screening, physical examination details.  
- No internal contradictions between transcript and DDx.  
- Transcript quality: Conversation clear and complete without significant speech disruption; minor audio cutting noted but no impact on data capture.
